summary.headline: Aarti Pharmalabs Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY to INR613 crores, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% and PAT at INR66 crores.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR613 crores (up 47% YoY from INR417 crores), with EBITDA of INR136 crores (up 84%) and PAT of INR66 crores versus INR24 crores a year earlier. Management attributed a few points of margin erosion to pass-through lag on elevated raw material costs, and Xanthine dispatches were held up by shipment issues (about 5% of quarter's Xanthine volume). Xanthine capacity ramp (nameplate 9,600 tonnes) and Atali Phase 1B trials are progressing, with full capitalisation of about INR300 crores CWIP expected by Q3 and year-end. Working capital rose on inventory and receivables, with cash conversion cycle cited at 150-160 days and short-term borrowings around INR650-660 crores per the analyst.

financial_highlights.value: Close to 165-167 days (management); 150-160 days cash conversion cycle (CFO)
financial_highlights.change: Higher on inventory build and receivables

segments.name: Xanthine derivatives and allied products
segments.commentary: 50% of turnover; beverages 62% and others 38% of volume; exports 59% and local 41%. Realisation up 10-15% YoY and average price up about 15% for the year; FY volume expected up 15-20% on last year's ~6,000 tonnes. Q2 Xanthine sales slightly lower on shipment holds while allied chemistry rose.

segments.name: API and intermediates
segments.commentary: 30% of turnover; split regulated 57%, ROW 33%, non-regulated 10%. Management says run-rate of INR180-200 crores can be the base for H2 every quarter; growth was largely volume-driven after steroid block debottlenecking.

segments.name: CDMO/CMO
segments.commentary: 13% of revenue; CDMO sales almost double Q1. 23 customers, 59 active projects (39 commercial, 20 development). Target 40-50% growth FY27 and INR1,000 crores revenue (or 100 million USD) target.

segments.name: Other sales
segments.commentary: 6% of revenue, including trading sales, export incentives and solvent and scrap sales.

guidance_outlook: Xanthine: full capacity ramp by end FY27; expected utilisation ~7,000 tonnes currently, 7,500-8,000 next year, up to ~8,800 within two years on 9,600 nameplate.
Atali Phase 1B to be capitalised in Q3; Atali block 2 targeted for commercialisation in H2 FY28; total capitalisation under INR300 crores with some spillover to Q1 FY28.
Management expects Q3/Q4 EBITDA margin to improve with higher CDMO mix and pass-through; about 1 percentage point improvement cited for H2 versus pass-through lag.
Company is maintaining 3-year guidance of 15-18% revenue and EBITDA growth; management declined to upgrade for FY27 specifically.
API and intermediate growth 10-15% annually plus new products; CDMO target INR1,000 crores revenue, with 10-12 projects of the 60 expected to drive INR700-800 crores.
Peptide and oligonucleotide lab expected operational by end FY27; customer business expected from FY28, no numerical guidance given.
capex_capacity: Xanthine expanded capacity: nameplate 9,600 tonnes; current utilisation near 7,000 tonnes; full capitalisation by end FY27.
Atali Phase 1A commercial scale-up line in commissioning; Phase 1B smaller line for early-stage projects in trials; expected to be fully utilised in H2 FY27.
Steroid API block capacity expansion completed and contributing to revenue; anti-cancer block 3 at Tarapur undergoing debottlenecking.
Atali block 2 groundbreaking done; commercialisation targeted H2 FY28. Management says new blocks deliver asset turn of 1.2-1.4x; no API business planned at Atali, only CDMO and intermediates.
Capex for FY27 targeted at INR350-400 crores, with about INR250 crores still to come in H2; management expects further debt to fund it.
demand_pricing: Raw material costs elevated due to geopolitical turmoil; company passing on increases to customers in Xanthine/allied and API.
Xanthine spot segment prices expected under pressure; pharma and beverage segments more stable; existing absolute margins expected to hold through FY28, per management.
API competition is both Chinese and Indian players; growth from new product launches with partners as patents expire and from alternate vendor development (AVD).
CDMO demand growth from China Plus One transfers; some projects are campaign-based with approval cycles.
API focus shifting to regulated markets with higher margins versus ROW and non-regulated.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Xanthine and Atali Phase 1 utilisation and CWIP of INR300 crores plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Xanthine to be fully capitalised by year-end; Atali Phase 1 complete, with capitalisation in Q3 after Phase 1B trials this week. Atali expected to be fully utilised in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will CDMO margins hold above 22-23% as Atali costs come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin % depends on raw material prices versus CDMO mix; absolute gross margin expected to keep rising, with H2 margin change of about 1 percentage point either way.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15-18% growth guidance be upgraded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is giving 3-year guidance and declined to give a pointed FY27 number, saying one year may be higher while the strategy is on track.

qa_highlights.question: How much Xanthine sales spilled over due to shipment issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 5% of the quarter's Xanthine volume, which management expects to clear in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need more debt for the remaining capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said more debt will be needed for the remaining FY27 capex of about INR250 crores; no separate figure given for the peak.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity beyond the new CDMO block?
qa_highlights.answer: Next year management will decide; more dedicated blocks possible if CDMO visibility rises. Xanthine capacity expansion not currently planned beyond 9,600 tonnes.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: inventory and receivables rose, cash flow from operations was low versus EBITDA, and short-term borrowings reportedly rose to around INR650-660 crores; more debt needed for remaining capex.
Xanthine spot-price pressure as crude and China export rebate withdrawal flow through; pass-through lag on raw material costs weighed on Q2 margins.
CDMO ramp dependence on customer approvals, campaign-based projects and launches (including Obicetrapib); management says timing may slip by a year.
Atali capitalisation spillover into Q1 FY28 and rising depreciation and opex in H2.
Peptide and oligonucleotide lab operational by end FY27; no revenue quantification yet, and R&D spend to rise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and CDMO trajectory, but evasive on specifics: declined to give FY27 guidance upgrade, Xanthine price breakup, peptide revenue and spot-versus-pharma split. Cautious on pricing, saying spot prices face pressure while raw material costs remain elevated.

We are presently working with 23 customers.
We remain on track to achieve our target of 40% to 50% revenue growth over last year on this business segment.
Overall, I think it is a fair idea that this 180-200 could be the base for second half every quarter.

adds.what: Xanthine expanded capacity, 9,600 tonnes nameplate (ramp, utilisation ~7,000 t)
Atali Phase 1B smaller line for early-stage projects (in trials, capitalise in Q3)
Peptide and oligonucleotide lab, operational by end FY27

growth.why: Management maintains a 3-year 15-18% revenue and EBITDA growth guide (not upgraded for FY27), with CDMO growth of 40-50% in FY27 and Xanthine volume up 15-20%, backed by Xanthine ramp on 9,600 t nameplate (~7,000 t utilised), Atali Phase 1B trials, and pricing pass-through, though Atali block 2 and peptide lab timelines run into FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects H2 EBITDA margin to improve about 1 percentage point from higher CDMO mix and pass-through, off a Q2 base of 22.2% (vs 17.7% a year ago), though raw material pass-through lag and spot pricing pressure cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Atali Phase 1B is to be capitalised in Q3 FY27 (about INR300 crores CWIP, with spillover possible into Q1 FY28), Xanthine 9,600 t nameplate is ramping to full capitalisation by end FY27, and Atali block 2 targets H2 FY28 commercialisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Xanthine FY volume guided up 15-20% on ~6,000 t last year, with utilisation rising from ~7,000 t toward 7,500-8,000 t next year, and CDMO growth of 40-50% in FY27 with 59 active projects.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Xanthine utilisation is ~7,000 t of 9,600 t nameplate (about 73%), Atali Phase 1 is fully used by H2 FY27 and management says more dedicated CDMO blocks are possible next year, though Xanthine expansion beyond 9,600 t is not planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 3-year 15-18% guide and declined to upgrade FY27 specifically; CDMO 40-50% growth and INR1,000 crore target were reiterated rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spot Xanthine prices face pressure, raw material costs remain elevated, CDMO timing may slip by a year on approvals, and Atali capitalisation may spill into Q1 FY28, with about 5% of Q2 Xanthine volume held in shipment.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Peptide and oligonucleotide lab operational by end FY27 with customer business from FY28, Atali block 2 commercialisation in H2 FY28, and new API products tied to patent expiries and CDMO launches (including Obicetrapib, which may slip a year).

rows.label: Working capital cycle and debt build
rows.why: Cash conversion cycle cited at 150-160 days (management says 165-167), short-term borrowings reportedly INR650-660 crores, and management says more debt is needed for the remaining ~INR250 crores of FY27 capex.

rows.label: API run-rate base for H2 at INR180-200 crores per quarter
rows.why: Management says the INR180-200 crore quarterly run-rate can be the base for H2, with API at 30% of turnover and regulated markets at 57% of API sales, supported by volume after steroid block debottlenecking.

rows.label: Xanthine spot price pressure
rows.why: Xanthine realisation rose 10-15% YoY and average price about 15% for the year, but spot segment prices are expected under pressure from crude and China export rebate withdrawal, while pharma and beverage segments remain more stable.
